questions.scenario: It's the Annual Sports Day at your school. What are you doing?

options.text: Running on the track, participating to win gold medals.
Standing on the sidelines, shouting strategies to your juniors.
Warming up, stretching, and keeping your body perfectly fit.
Helping the teachers arrange the trophies, scoreboards, and crowd.
Standing by with the first-aid kit, ready to treat any sprains, cramps, or injuries.
None of these.

questions.scenario: You are playing a sports video game (like FIFA, Cricket 24, or NBA). What's your favorite part?

options.text: Playing the actual match and scoring the winning points.
Setting the team formation, tactics, and field placements.
Upgrading the players' stamina, strength, and health stats.
Playing 'Career Mode' to buy/sell players and manage club budgets.
Checking the injury reports and managing the recovery timelines of my star players.
None of these.

questions.scenario: When you watch a live cricket or football match on TV, what do you notice the most?

options.text: The magic of the perfect shot, catch, or goal.
Why the captain made a specific bowling/passing change.
The incredible muscles, speed, and endurance of the players.
The stadium crowd, the sponsors, and how huge the event is.
How a player recovers after a bad fall and the physio team rushing to the field.
None of these.

questions.scenario: A friend tells you, 'I want to get fit and lose weight.' How do you help?

options.text: Challenge them to play a sport with you every evening.
Teach them the correct running technique so they don't get injured.
Make a strict daily workout chart and protein diet plan for them.
Find the best gym deals nearby and organize their schedule.
Check their posture and joint health first to ensure they don't get hurt while exercising.
None of these.

questions.scenario: Your team is losing badly at half-time. What is your reaction?

options.text: Push my own physical limits even harder in the second half.
Give a motivational speech and change the team's strategy.
Give the team energy drinks and quick muscle massages.
Keep the sponsors and audience engaged so the event doesn't flop.
Tape up the players' minor injuries, apply ice packs, and reduce their physical pain.
None of these.

questions.scenario: What kind of YouTube video would you click on instantly?

options.text: Top 10 Insane Impossible Goals/Shots in History.
How the Underdog Team's Captain planned the greatest victory.
Virat Kohli or Cristiano Ronaldo's secret diet and gym routine.
How the IPL makes Thousands of Crores every year.
Worst Sports Injuries and How the Athletes Recovered miraculously.
None of these.

questions.scenario: What gives you the greatest feeling of satisfaction?

options.text: Hearing the crowd scream my name after I win.
Seeing someone I taught achieve their biggest dream.
Looking in the mirror and seeing physical progress.
Successfully organizing a massive tournament with zero mistakes.
Helping an injured athlete walk, run, or play again after a terrible accident.
None of these.

questions.scenario: Every sports career has a 'boring/hard' part. Which one can you tolerate easily?

options.text: Practicing the exact same shot/move 1,000 times a day.
Watching hours of boring match videos to find the opponent's weakness.
Eating boring boiled food and giving up tasty junk food completely.
Doing math, counting ticket sales, and calling angry sponsors.
Studying complex human anatomy books and memorizing every bone and muscle.
None of these.

questions.scenario: A new modern sports complex opens in your city. What catches your eye first?

options.text: The beautiful turf/court where I can play matches.
The training academies and how the instructors are teaching.
The heavy weights, treadmills, and high-tech gym machines.
The membership fees, marketing posters, and daily crowd.
The recovery section with ice baths, massage tables, and physiotherapy equipment.
None of these.

questions.scenario: In any sports group, what is your ultimate title?

options.text: The Star (The one who performs).
The Mentor (The one who guides).
The Beast (The fittest and strongest).
The Boss (The one who runs the show).
The Healer (The one who knows exactly what to do when someone gets hurt).
None of these.
